name: Question 20
worked_solution:
First, we note that 

$$
F(t)=\int {F}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t=\int ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,,{sec}^{2}⁡(t)⟩\text{d}t.
$$

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,,{sec}^{2}⁡(t)⟩\text{d}t & =⟨\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\,\text{d}t,\int {sec}^{2}⁡(t)\,\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+{c}_{1},\,\operatorname{tan}⁡(t)+{c}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The initial condition $F(\frac{\pi }{4})=⟨1,\,0⟩$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}F(\frac{\pi }{4})=⟨\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})+{c}_{1},\,\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})+{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨1,\,0⟩ \\ ⟨\frac{1}{2}+{c}_{1},\,1+{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨1,\,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${c}_{1}=\frac{1}{2}$ and ${c}_{2}=-1.$ Consequently

$$
F(t)=⟨\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)+\frac{1}{2},\,\operatorname{tan}⁡(t)-1⟩.
$$

Question 20
?

If F′(t)=⟨cos⁡(2t),sec2⁡(t)⟩ and F(π4)=⟨1,0⟩, then F(t)=

a
⟨cos⁡(t)+1,2sec⁡(t)−1⟩
b
⟨12sin⁡(2t)+12,tan⁡(t)⟩
c
⟨12cos⁡(t)−12,2sec⁡(t)+2⟩
d
⟨12sin⁡(2t)+12,tan⁡(t)−1⟩
e
⟨sin⁡(2t)−1,tan⁡(t)−1⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that

F(t)=∫F′(t)dt=∫⟨cos⁡(2t),sec2⁡(t)⟩dt.

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we have

∫⟨cos⁡(2t),sec2⁡(t)⟩dt=⟨∫cos⁡(2t)dt,∫sec2⁡(t)dt⟩=⟨12sin⁡(2t)+c1,tan⁡(t)+c2⟩.

The initial condition F(π4)=⟨1,0⟩ gives

F(π4)=⟨12sin⁡(π2)+c1,tan⁡(π4)+c2⟩=⟨1,0⟩⟨12+c1,1+c2⟩=⟨1,0⟩.

Therefore, c1=12 and c2=−1. Consequently

F(t)=⟨12sin⁡(2t)+12,tan⁡(t)−1⟩.
